hook: Both ORMs are free, and in 2026 each arrives with a database vendor attached: Prisma sells Prisma Postgres beside its client, and PlanetScale hired Drizzle's entire core team in March. The choice is no longer generated client versus SQL builder; it is who ends up holding your data layer.

sections.title: Both ORMs are free, so the price is who holds your data layer
Prisma 7 turns the compiled client into rules your old schema breaks
Drizzle forbids a stable 1.0, Studio source and a neutral owner
sections.content:
Drizzle's philosophy costs nothing at runtime. It bills you in dependency risk instead.

- **No stable 1.0.** 1.0.0-rc.5 shipped 21 October 2026, and its notes list a dozen-plus BREAKING changes, from postgres-js parsers to `withReplicas` default routing and the `sqlite-proxy` rework.
- **No Studio source.** ORM and Kit are open source; Drizzle Studio is not.
- **No neutral owner.** In March 2026 PlanetScale hired the entire core team. Drizzle's own page: "PlanetScale is our biggest sponsor, they hired us".

That is a hire, not an acquisition, and the code stays open source. Still, the people choosing the next routing default are paid by a database company.

> Pin the exact RC, because a version range on a candidate lets the next BREAKING list in unannounced.

sections.title: Prisma's "90% smaller" client booted 3.4x slower in one developer's test
sections.content:
Two kinds of evidence disagree here. **Vendor claim:** 90% smaller output and 3x faster queries, from a Rust engine of roughly 14 MB (7 MB gzipped) to a compiler of about 1.6 MB (600 KB gzipped).

Alex Georgiev's test, published 6 November 2026, ran two identical SQLite projects on one local machine. One developer, not a lab.

| Measure | Prisma 6.19.3 | Prisma 7.10.1 |
|---|---|---|
| Warm `findUnique`, 2,000 calls | ~0.60 ms each | ~0.19 ms each |
| Process start to first query | ~69 ms | ~236 ms |
| `node_modules` | 254.1 MiB | 333.3 MiB |

The warm row backs the vendor: 0.60 ÷ 0.19 ≈ 3.1x. The cold row runs the other way, mostly in `import` and `$connect()`. Both hold at once: the compiler shrank, yet per-database WASM builds in two sizes grew `node_modules` 31%.

sections.title: Prisma Postgres punishes chatty code, and its cheap plan stops being cheap below 6M queries
sections.content:
Prisma Postgres bills one query as one operation, a unit that punishes N+1 loops and polling, not storage or seats.

| Plan | Base | Included | Overage |
|---|---|---|---|
| Starter | $10 | 1M ops | $8 per million |
| Pro | $49 | 10M ops | $2 per million |
| Business | $129 | 50M ops | $1 per million |

Starter meets Pro where $10 + $8 × (n − 1) = $49, so n = 5.875M operations a month. Above that, the $49 plan is cheaper.

At 20M operations, Starter costs $10 + 19 × $8 = $162 and Pro costs $49 + 10 × $2 = $69. That $93 monthly gap comes from moving one plan up, not from new infrastructure.

One line item is retiring: the Accelerate cache ends 1 December 2026. If it absorbed your reads, redo the crossover with the uncached query count.

sections.title: Drizzle's meter reads $0, so the bill moves to whoever employs its team
sections.content:
Drizzle charges $0 for the ORM, Kit, Studio for local development and Gateway. The cost has not vanished: you pay the database vendor directly, and since March 2026 one such vendor employs the maintainers.

- Pick **Drizzle** when you want no codegen and can pin a release candidate.
- Pick **Prisma** when one bill for database plus runtime beats an RC branch, and your workload is many warm queries rather than many cold starts.

Check before your next deploy:

1. Count monthly queries and place yourself against the 5.875M crossover.
2. Time process start to first query on your own target before trusting either Prisma figure.
3. On Drizzle, confirm `package.json` pins 1.0.0-rc.5 exactly, not a range.

decision_matrix.situation: Serverless functions where cold starts dominate, currently on Prisma 6
decision_matrix.pick: Neither — stay on Prisma 6 until you measure 7
decision_matrix.why: One developer's SQLite test measured about 69 ms to first query on 6.19.3 against about 236 ms on 7.10.1.

decision_matrix.situation: Long-running API server issuing many warm queries
decision_matrix.why: The same test reproduced the vendor's 3x on warm lookups, about 0.60 ms against 0.19 ms per findUnique.

decision_matrix.situation: Team policy forbids release candidates in production
decision_matrix.why: Drizzle's newest release on 10 November 2026 is 1.0.0-rc.5, not a stable 1.0.

decision_matrix.situation: TypeScript-only codebase where a codegen step keeps breaking CI
decision_matrix.why: The TypeScript file is the schema, so there is no generator output to keep in sync.

decision_matrix.situation: Already running PlanetScale and happy to deepen that relationship
decision_matrix.why: PlanetScale employs the core team, so the ORM's sponsor and your database vendor are the same company.

decision_matrix.situation: Want one invoice for managed Postgres plus the runtime
decision_matrix.why: Prisma sells Prisma Postgres and Prisma Compute on the same pricing page, next to a free ORM.

decision_matrix.situation: Need an ORM whose maintainers no database vendor pays
decision_matrix.pick: Neither — pin a version and keep the exit path documented
decision_matrix.why: Prisma sells its own database and PlanetScale hired Drizzle's team, so neither option is vendor-neutral in 2026.

decision_matrix.situation: Prisma app with hot paths already written as raw SQL
decision_matrix.why: From 7.3.0, $queryRaw and $executeRaw bypass the query compiler and go straight to the driver adapter.

cost_math.label: Prisma Postgres Starter vs Pro crossover
cost_math.result: Above 5.875M operations a month, Pro at $49 is cheaper than Starter

cost_math.label: Prisma Compute, one always-on small service

verdict_summary: Drizzle wins if you want no codegen step and can pin 1.0.0-rc.5 in production, accepting that PlanetScale now employs its maintainers. Prisma wins if one bill for database plus runtime beats tracking an RC branch and your workload is many warm queries rather than many cold starts. If cold starts dominate, time Prisma 7.10.1 against 6.19.3 on your own target before upgrading.

faqs.q: Do I have to use Prisma Postgres to use Prisma ORM?
faqs.a: No: the ORM is free on every plan and works without Prisma Postgres. If you do try the database, its Free plan includes 200,000 operations with the spend limit fixed at $0 and no card.

faqs.q: Can I shrink the Prisma 7 query compiler?
faqs.a: Since 7.3.0 the generator accepts `compilerBuild = "fast" | "small"`, with `fast` as the default. In Alex Georgiev's listing the SQLite compiler is 4,406,183 bytes in the fast build and 2,214,935 bytes in the small one.

faqs.q: Will long-running queries survive Prisma Postgres connection pooling?
faqs.a: Pooled connections run in transaction mode with a 10-minute query duration limit and a 60-minute idle timeout. Pooled connection caps are 10, 100, 500 and 1,000 from Free to Business, with 10, 10, 50 and 100 direct connections.

faqs.q: Which databases can Drizzle talk to?
faqs.a: Postgres, MySQL, SQLite, SingleStore, MSSQL and CockroachDB, through the standard drivers. Drizzle states the ORM has "exactly 0 dependencies".
